title: Sydney Lucas Arrest – Body-Worn Camera and Video Records

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Florida Sunshine Law, I hereby request the following records:

Incident date: August 21, 2026
Individual involved: Sydney Lucas
Location: Irish Kevin’s, 211 Duval Street, Key West, Florida

All publicly releasable audiovisual and photographic records relating to the Key West Police Department incident and arrest involving Sydney Lucas on August 21, 2026, at or near Irish Kevin’s on Duval Street.

Specifically:

• Complete, unedited body-worn camera (BWC) footage from every KWPD officer who responded to, participated in, assisted with, transported, or documented the incident/arrest.
• All dash-camera/in-car video and associated audio from police vehicles involved.
• All surveillance/security-camera footage obtained by KWPD, including footage received from Irish Kevin’s or surrounding businesses.
• All photographs, videos, and audiovisual evidence collected or created by KWPD in connection with the incident, including photographs/scans/video of the allegedly fraudulent identification and other physical evidence.
• Any available audio/video of transportation or transfer of custody following the arrest maintained by KWPD.
• The corresponding incident/offense report, arrest/probable-cause affidavit, supplemental reports, and CAD/dispatch report, including records identifying all responding officers.

Please provide video in its original electronic format and highest reasonably available quality, rather than screenshots or transcripts. If portions are exempt, please provide all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions and identify the statutory basis for any redactions or withholding.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Nick Wong

title: Subject: APRA Request — AXON Body-Camera Recordings, Evidence and Device Audit Trails, and Related Records — True Initial Response, Call #25-14916

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Rhode Island Access to Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Subject: APRA Request — AXON Body-Camera Recordings, Evidence and Device Audit Trails, and Related Records — True Initial Response, Call #25-14916

To the Scituate Police Department Public Records Officer:

Pursuant to the Rhode Island Access to Public Records Act, R.I. Gen. Laws § 38-2-1 et seq., I request the existing records identified below concerning the body-worn camera footage of the true first initial response associated with Call for Service #25-14916.

This request specifically seeks AXON records, including both Evidence Audit Trails and Device Audit Trails. CAD logs alone will not satisfy it.

This is a separate request that supplements, and does not withdraw, supersede, or waive, my earlier requests or appeals concerning these records.

Identification of the incident

My June 11, 2026 correspondence identified the initial response as occurring at approximately 10:04 a.m. on November 30, 2025, at or near 141 Nipmuc Road, involving Joshua Grissom. The June 29 request subsequently contained a conflicting reference to November 30, 2024.

Please use Call for Service #25-14916 and the Department’s existing incident records to identify the correct event. Please flag and resolve the inconsistent year rather than treating it as a reason to overlook the identifiable call.

The Department’s May 14, 2026 revised estimate identified Sergeant Clayton’s body-camera footage and associated Axon audit trails for this initial call. Include records for any other officer who actually participated in that initial response.

Search linked or alternative identifiers, including Call for Service #25-14919, where necessary to identify the initial footage, distinguish it from follow-up footage, or trace a recording that was mislabeled or reassigned. Later footage is not a substitute for the actual initial-response footage.

Time periods

For the recordings, the requested event runs from the initial response through completion of that first call, including first arrival, first contact, and the initial statement or complaint.

For device activity, include the entire incident date and the relevant shift, including any adjacent-date portion of that shift and the next docking or upload session.

For evidence handling, access, retention, deletion, restriction, sharing, and related administrative records, include the history from creation of the relevant material through the date the Department receives this request. Do not limit those histories to activity occurring on the incident date; later handling is also requested.

Records requested

1. Initial-response recordings and identifying metadata

Provide all existing body-camera video and audio segments documenting the initial response, including short, interrupted, separately stored, or uncategorized segments and any saved pre-event footage.

Provide full-length recordings in an ordinarily available export format, subject to lawful redactions, rather than selected clips or summaries alone.

Include existing metadata identifying the evidence UUID/ID, original and current title or filename, recording start and end times, duration, upload time, recording officer, device serial number, associated call or case identifiers, and any existing file-integrity hash or checksum. Preserve available time-zone and timestamp information.

Where a released copy is redacted, clipped, or otherwise derived from another file, include the existing records linking that copy to its source.

2. Complete Axon Evidence Audit Trails and relevant Case Audit Trails

Provide the complete available Evidence Audit Trail for each responsive recording, including any recording previously represented to me or my attorney as the initial-call footage.

Also provide relevant Case Audit Trail entries showing how those recordings were associated with, added to, removed from, or moved between cases.

Include all available event types and all relevant users or automated-system activity—not merely selected entries. The requested history includes creation, upload, viewing, modification, renaming, reassignment, categorization, retention changes, restriction, redaction, sharing, export, deletion, and restoration.

Include surviving histories for responsive items that are now deleted, restricted, archived, or otherwise unavailable. Use the full requested period, not a default recent-date window.

3. Complete Axon Device Audit Trails and related device logs

Provide the Device Audit Trail for each body camera assigned to an officer participating in the initial response during the device-activity period specified above.

Include existing device-event, diagnostic, and upload records reflecting, where generated and retained: power changes; recording starts and stops; audio muting or reactivation; activation triggers; buffering settings or events; errors; battery or storage status; clock changes; docking; upload completion or failure; and removal of local files.

Please provide the available standard PDF and CSV exports. I am requesting the event information actually supported and retained by the relevant camera model and firmware, not assuming that every model generates every type of event.

4. Officer/device assignments, recording inventories, and relevant user activity

Provide existing records identifying which officers and body cameras were assigned to the initial response, including device model, serial number, relevant firmware information, and any replacement or reassignment during the shift.

Provide existing recording lists, device profiles, or ordinary system exports identifying the files created by those cameras during the requested device-activity period, including evidence identifiers, recording times, and upload status. This inventory request does not seek the video content of unrelated calls.

Include relevant Axon user or administrator audit entries concerning the responsive evidence, its device assignments, access restrictions, or handling. I am not requesting unrelated agency-wide user activity.

5. Retention, restriction, deletion, restoration, and preservation records

Provide existing records concerning the retention or disposition of responsive footage and its audit information, including applicable retention categories and settings, changes to those settings, holds and their removal, archival, restrictions on access, and scheduled or completed deletion.

Include any related request, authorization, approval, denial, automated action, purge entry, restoration entry, or record identifying the responsible user or system and the date of the action.

Please distinguish, through the records maintained, between material that was never recorded, not uploaded, mislabeled, restricted, archived, deleted, transferred, or simply not located.

The absence of an available video file should not end the search for surviving records documenting what happened to it.

6. Copies, exports, sharing, discovery, and prior productions

Provide existing export manifests, sharing records, delivery records, package inventories, redaction records, and other records identifying which responsive recordings or versions were provided to prosecutors, defense counsel, other agencies, or in response to records requests.

Include available evidence identifiers and source-to-copy links sufficient to determine whether material previously described as initial-call footage was the actual initial response or a later recording.

This includes relevant share-by-reference, share-copy, and download records where maintained. I am not requesting privileged legal advice.

7. Missing-footage explanations, supervisory review, and corrective or disciplinary records

Provide existing records concerning any failure to activate a camera, interruption or premature termination of recording, muting, malfunction, upload failure, missing footage, misidentification, unauthorized alteration, or improper deletion associated with this initial response.

Include relevant officer explanations, report passages, supervisor notifications and reviews, technical-support tickets, communications with Axon or other relevant service providers, and the records previously described by the Department as “Initial Discovery Issue Records.”

Also include related complaints, referrals, investigative records, findings, dispositions, and records of actual corrective measures, retraining, or disciplinary action, to the extent releasable. Include a recorded determination that no violation occurred or no action was warranted, if such a record exists.

Unlike the report exclusion in my June 29 request, this request includes the portions of reports and administrative records documenting the recording’s existence, absence, interruption, malfunction, or handling. It does not seek unrelated personnel or medical records.

I am requesting existing documentation, not directing the Department to initiate a new investigation or create findings.

8. Applicable policies and retention schedules

Provide the versions of the Department’s body-camera and digital-evidence policies applicable on the incident date and during subsequent handling of these records, including General Order 310.07 and relevant amendments with their effective dates.

Include applicable policies or schedules governing recording, deactivation, muting, upload, supervisory review, access auditing, restrictions, deletion authorization, evidence retention, and audit-log retention, including the applicable version of Records Retention Schedule LG6.3.6.

Please include existing configuration or policy records identifying the retention rules actually applied to this footage and its associated logs.

9. Existing records of searches for the initial footage

Provide existing search records, correspondence, notes, or support records documenting efforts to locate the true initial-response footage or explain why it was not previously produced.

This includes existing records concerning whether follow-up footage was identified or supplied as the initial response, and records connecting the disputed footage to a different evidence identifier, call number, officer account, device, or storage location.

Search, production, and exemptions

Please search responsive records within the Department’s custody or control, including its agency-accessible Axon Evidence/Evidence.com environment, relevant restricted or archived items, and retained local or vendor-hosted records maintained on its behalf.

An appropriately authorized person should conduct the search where ordinary user permissions would otherwise prevent access. Search by relevant device, officer, recording time, and alternative identifiers where a call-number-only search would omit untagged or mislabeled evidence.

I am requesting existing records and ordinary exports of stored data, not creation of a new narrative, custom software, or forensic reconstruction of information that no longer exists.

Please provide electronic records in their existing or ordinarily exportable formats. Produce available audit and identification records separately from video so that review of the footage does not unnecessarily delay the non-video portion.

For any withholding or redaction, provide the specific statutory basis and explanation, and release reasonably segregable non-exempt information. A determination about the video itself should not automatically be applied to every associated log or administrative record.

Where records in a requested category do not exist or are not within the Department’s custody or control, state that in writing under § 38-2-7(c). Please make clear which category the determination addresses.

Fees and preservation

If charges would exceed $25, provide an itemized good-faith estimate before incurring charges above that amount. Separate the estimate for audit logs and metadata from video review/redaction and other administrative records. Identify the work, estimated hours, and rates, and apply the statutory fee limitations and free search time to the extent applicable.

For comparable audit exports previously identified in the May 14, 2026 estimate, please explain any material increase in estimated processing time, distinguishing the additional history requested here from the previously identified records.

Please preserve the responsive original recordings, metadata, logs, existing copies, and disposition records while this request and any resulting review remain pending, including responsive material awaiting routine deletion.

This request concerns public oversight of body-camera use and evidence handling and is not made for commercial purposes. Please respond within the time required by APRA, including a particularized written explanation of any extension claimed.

Sincerely,
Joshua Grissom

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Josh Grissom

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I am requesting access to and copies of records held by the National Archives and Records Administration that were identified by the Federal Bureau of Investigation as responsive to my FOIPA request but transferred to NARA custody rather than processed directly by the FBI.

By letter dated September 18, 2026 (FOIPA Request No. 1755138-000, Subject: "Revolutionary War Organization"), the FBI's Record/Information Dissemination Section advised that records potentially responsive to my request were transferred to NARA, and directed me to reference the following FBI file numbers, all bearing FBI Classification 100 (Domestic Security), found within Record Group 65, Records of the Federal Bureau of Investigation:

● 100-HQ-452863
● 100-HQ-473049
● 100-HQ-442715
● 100-HQ-442786
● 100-HQ-6877

● 100-NY-148047-3070
● 100-NY-161514
● 100-NY-167072
● 100-HQ-455011

A copy of the document can be found online here: 
https://cdn.muckrock.com/foia_files/2026/09/21/E13d990ba39b6e32a28bbd3f319338954c77ac165da427a85d9_Q341556_D165960914.pdf

I ask that NARA search the Classification 100 (Domestic Security) Headquarters Case Files series for the "HQ" numbers listed above, and the corresponding New York Field Office Case Files series for the "NY" numbers, and provide copies of all file units associated with each number. If any of these numbers (particularly 100-HQ-3-65, given its unusually low base file number) correspond to a general or umbrella file to which sub-files or cross-references relating
to the "Revolutionary War Organization" (also referenced in some records as "Revolutionary War Organizations") were later appended, I request that NARA identify the specific sub-file(s) or serials pertaining to that organization and process those portions.

If any portion of this request is denied, please provide a description of each withheld record, the specific exemption(s) claimed, and segregate and release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions.
